B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee. Successful MCP tool calls use two tasks from the Zapier account’s plan allowance; failed calls do not use tasks. The Free plan lists 100 tasks/month, so at the stated rate that allowance covers up to 50 successful MCP calls if none is used elsewhere. Paid plans and pay-per-task billing may provide additional usage.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Zapier lists Free at $0/month with 100 tasks/month; Professional and Team are paid plans, and Enterprise pricing is by quote. Prices for paid plans are not recorded here because the official pricing page is dynamically rendered and the available text did not provide stable amounts.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP calls draw from the same task allowance as other Zapier products. Two tasks per successful call; failed calls do not count. No per-session call limit is documented. Pay-per-task billing, where enabled, can charge for overage up to the configured cap; otherwise calls stop at the task limit.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: MCP is enabled by default at account level. Workspace admins can enable or disable it, restrict users, and set workspace task quotas. Server sharing requires Team or Enterprise; tool bundles can be shared on any plan. Transport is Streamable HTTP only, not SSE. A successful tool call consumes plan tasks.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Zapier controls account service and billing; account/workspace owners and admins control workspace availability, user access, quotas, and account restrictions; server owners configure tools and connections.

Managed mode exposes each configured app action as its own tool. Early Access adds workflow tools; write_code_action is described as rolling out. The successful tool list depends on server mode, account access, enabled tools, connections, and feature availability.

C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration endpoint advertised; Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants; PKCE S256; supported scopes: openid, profile, email; token auth methods: none, client_secret_post, client_secret_basic. Revocation endpoint advertised, and docs say the OAuth connection can be revoked from the client or Zapier; rotating/revoking a connection token cuts off clients using it.

The endpoint has two server modes and dynamically selectable app actions. Agentic mode offers skills, which are saved Markdown workflow instructions that the agent loads on demand. Managed mode exposes a fixed set of configured action tools and makes skills unavailable. Early Access workflow tools build and manage Next Gen Zaps. A feedback tool sends feedback to Zapier.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Skills return Markdown instructions; workflow tools return workflow/draft/run records, including run identifiers and output. Complete response schemas not published.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official tools include read/search and write/action-management tools; workflow tools include create, update, delete, enable, run, publish, and draft operations. The docs do not publish MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). 2. No universal server-enforced user confirmation step is documented. Zapier lets operators fix/limit field values, and product/app permissions still apply. The public client plugin recommends confirmation before writes, but that is client guidance, not evidence of endpoint enforcement. 3. OAuth metadata advertises identity scopes openid, profile, email; authorization-code and refresh-token grants; PKCE S256; DCR and revocation endpoints. Docs also describe per-server connection tokens. Zapier/account/workspace and connected-app permissions apply; user connections are not shared with other users. Workspace admins can set quotas/restrict users; owners/superadmins can inspect all servers. 4. Agentic mode supports dynamic discovery; managed mode fixes the action set and prevents the agent enabling new actions. Admin and operator field restrictions apply. Streamable HTTP only; no SSE. No region-specific endpoint documented. 5. Docs describe logical account segregation, US-East-1 storage, role-based/network controls, and Enterprise training opt-out; no MCP-specific PII masking or field redaction documented. 6. Two tasks per successful tool call; no session call/tool limit; task allowance and optional pay-per-task billing govern use. No result truncation cap found. Workflow output may be condensed by default, with full operations journal via include_results. 7. Operator-set field values override client values; allowed-choice restrictions constrain dropdown values. No generic argument-alias correction or schema behavior documented. 8. Tool calls appear in server History and account audit log. Enterprise history retention is configurable. Terms say Zapier may use usage information to improve services and derived de-identified data; Enterprise data is opted out of AI model training by default. 9. send_feedback is an official tool that sends feedback to Zapier. No tool-result upsell was found in official tool descriptions. 10. The server delivers saved and packaged skills in agentic mode; skill directions are instructions to the client, not server-enforced policies. Public client plugin contains additional lifecycle/read-write guidance. 11. Server state includes configured apps/actions, skills, clients, and call history. Those settings affect tools and connections available to subsequent calls; exact adaptive behavior is not documented. 12. Non-flat structure: two modes, configurable/dynamically discovered app-action tools, optional workflow tools, and multiple MCP clients on a shared server. 13. write_code_action is a documented, rollout-dependent custom-code action executed in a sandbox with authenticated API access; it is an extensible action path. No general raw HTTP, SQL, or shell tool is documented.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: “Before building or modifying a workflow, your agent reads the zapier:build-workflows skill with get_zapier_skill.”

“Before building or modifying a workflow, your agent reads the zapier:build-workflows skill with get_zapier_skill. Several workflow tools link to this skill directly in their descriptions, so most agents load it automatically.”

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The endpoint offers a dynamic agentic mode and a fixed managed mode; workflow and code-action tools are conditional, and one server can serve multiple MCP clients. These modes change the tool surface presented to clients.

E_aggregated.action_count: 16 static agentic-mode meta-tools by default; +25 Early Access workflow tools when available; +1 rollout-dependent write_code_action. Managed mode instead exposes a variable number of configured action tools.
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Official tool reference: https://docs.zapier.com/mcp/overview/how-tools-work names 16 static meta-tools and 25 Early Access workflow tools, plus a rollout-dependent write_code_action. The official list is conditional/configurable, not a fixed inventory of all app actions: managed mode exposes configured app actions individually, and the published sources do not enumerate all 40,000+ app actions. actions.json lists all 42 official names located (16 + 25 + 1); workflow/code tools are marked conditional. No catalogue-only tools added. MartechDB reported 17 tools on 2026-10-27, consistent with 16 base tools plus rollout-dependent write_code_action. MCP.so said its tool list was unavailable; APIs.io described dynamic discovery without enumerating names; API Tracker reported registry metadata and no inspected tool list; Vetted.tools did not provide additional native tool names.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server is closed and does not publish complete tool definitions, input schemas, or initialize instructions. The public repository is a client-side plugin distribution and not the endpoint implementation; therefore a token count for the endpoint context cannot be computed.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Humans can change server mode, select and configure actions, set fixed or constrained field values, and manage app connections in the Zapier dashboard. The endpoint provides configuration tools but documentation describes field/mode management as dashboard operations. Ordinary Zap building, integration setup, account administration, and app-directory action discovery remain broader Zapier product surfaces; MCP is limited to configured/discoverable actions and conditional Next Gen workflow tools. The full set of human-only operations is not enumerated in the reviewed sources.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Zapier’s client plugin recommends asking the user before write actions and presenting the exact action and relevant payload. This is client-side guidance; the hosted server docs do not describe a server-enforced confirmation requirement. The docs say agents should load the workflow skill before creating/modifying workflows; that is behavior guidance and tool descriptions, not an enforcement guarantee.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Official docs state: “Zapier MCP automatically enforces any app and action restrictions set at the account level.” They also say app permissions apply, MCP events appear in audit logs, and Enterprise retention is configurable. The data-retention schedule says MCP prompts/responses and tool-execution history remain until the associated MCP server or account is deleted, then are removed from backups within four months. Enterprise customers are opted out of AI model training by default. Zapier’s Terms permit processing customer content as reasonably necessary to operate, maintain, improve, and update the service, and permit use of usage information and derived de-identified data.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Zapier says it handles app credentials so MCP clients do not handle third-party API keys. Its documentation describes logical account segregation, app-level permission inheritance, workspace controls, and SOC 2 Type II certification. It states that tool bundles share tool configuration but not connected accounts or data.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Account/app permission inheritance, field-value overrides, task metering, and dashboard history are described as operational controls. The public implementation is unavailable, so server-side enforcement details cannot be independently inspected. Write confirmation appears only in the client plugin guidance, not as a documented server rule. Retention, training, and data-handling statements are governance documentation; no MCP-specific PII-masking mechanism is documented.

contradictions: Official docs state 16 always-available agentic meta-tools and separately describe write_code_action as available only on some servers during rollout. MartechDB reported 17 tools on 2026-10-27; this appears to count the rollout-dependent tool alongside the 16, rather than establish a different complete tool list.

The endpoint-specific protected-resource metadata advertises only openid, profile, and email scopes. The product documentation describes broader app actions, but says calls use existing app connections and product/app permissions. The metadata scopes appear to authorize identity access, not enumerate app-operation scopes; this distinction is not explained in the metadata itself.

Official documentation says new servers default to agentic mode, with some programmatic/non-conversational clients starting in managed mode. Consequently, the default tool surface varies by client and server configuration.
observations_for_research: The agentic tool surface supports in-conversation discovery and enabling of additional actions; managed mode moves action selection to the dashboard and fixes the set available to the client.
Operator-configured field values can override values supplied by the MCP client, and dropdown choices on write actions can be constrained.
Skills are stored per server and shared across clients attached to that server; they are unavailable in managed mode.
The account permission model delegates app/action restrictions to account controls and connected app permissions rather than introducing MCP-only action restrictions.
Successful calls incur two Zapier plan tasks, connecting the server’s access model to the vendor’s general usage meter.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, the full collected official docs pages and scripts, pricing and legal pages, third-party catalogues, endpoint captures, and the local official GitHub repository. The endpoint returned 401 without credentials; no login or authenticated tools/list request was made. The published repository is plugin/configuration content, not the deployed server. Official docs name the stable and conditional meta-tools but do not publish their input schemas or the complete personalized app-action inventory. The MCP Registry URL in the evidence folder returned 404. Third-party catalogues were used only to cross-check counts; their abstract dynamic-discovery descriptions were not treated as native tool names. The collected docs also identify a separate docs-search MCP, excluded from this endpoint’s actions.
